head.citation-title: Experimental and numerical investigation for the flexural behavior of pretensioned spun precast concrete piles
head.abstracts: © 2025 Elsevier LtdPretensioned Spun Precast Concrete (SPC) piles are considered to be a good solution for deep foundations because of their easier installation, superior quality control, cleaner manufacturing processes, reduced material used, and overall economic efficiency. However, the reduced sectional area of SPC piles resulting from their hollowness and usually a low percentage of prestressing strands raises concerns about their flexural capacity, particularly in seismic areas where both strength and ductility are important for the foundation's resilience. In this regard, the flexural response of SPC Piles was investigated both experimentally and numerically. Nine full-scale SPC pile specimens were tested under four-point bending until complete failure occurred. The specimen variations encompass two different diameters, numbers of strands, and thicknesses. The moment-deformation responses, fracture propagation, failure patterns, deformed configurations, and load-strain responses were examined meticulously. Subsequently, the flexural response of the specimens was analyzed parametrically using the finite element (FE) method, following the requisite validation of the FE models. The parameters analyzed were concrete grade, spiral spacing, number of strands, effective prestress, and thickness-to-diameter ratio. The experimental results suggest that increasing the sectional size from 300 mm to 400 mm increases the bending capacity by 64 % and deformation capacity by 50 % whereas increasing the number of strands has very little influence on the bending capacity. The parametric analysis suggested that the flexural performance and materials use of SPC piles were optimum with an effective prestress of 6.0 MPa and a thickness-to-diameter (t/D) ratio of 0.20–0.23. Comparison with design codes showed that the PCI guideline provided the most accurate ultimate moment predictions with a mean ratio = 1.21 and SD = 0.09. Moreover, pile capacity improves with the increase in concrete grade, though brittle failure occurs when these values exceed 50 MPa. Therefore, this study provides insight into the flexural response of SPC Pile specimens, facilitating their application in earthquake zones.
